_comment: Guided tour for the H2MM tool. Hand-built Qt around a DockArea, so steps target the shared action buttons by objectName suffix ({'name': 'run'} finds toolAction_run), the tool-specific buttons by their tooltip text ({'action': 'LL scan'}), and the result plots by dock tab title. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: From "it moved" to how fast, and into what
steps.text:
BVA and 2CDE say a burst changed. H2MM says into how many states, at what efficiencies, and with what rate constants — fitted to the raw photon record.

There is no bin anywhere. The inter-photon time is the timing observable: across a gap of Δt ticks the hidden chain takes Δt unobserved steps, so the propagator is the matrix power AΔt. Every photon contributes its colour and its gap; nothing is discarded and no arbitrary timescale is imposed.

Eight steps.

steps.title: The burst folder
steps.text: H2MM fits the photons inside already-defined bursts, so it reads a finished burst-analysis folder rather than raw files. Dropping the folder on this window does the same thing.

await.hint: Press the folder button and choose the burst-analysis folder.

steps.title: Which detector is which — and the third stream
steps.text:
Donor and acceptor come from the detector setup here. With µsALEX or PIE data, define the acceptor-excitation stream as well: it gives every state a stoichiometry, which is what separates a real conformational state from acceptor photophysics on the E–S map.

Get the assignment backwards and the fit still converges, still reports states, and still looks plausible.

steps.title: How many states — and why the answer gets conservative fast
steps.text:
Raw likelihood always rises with K, so the state count is decided by a penalised criterion. BIC penalises parameters; ICL also penalises states that overlap, so it rewards models whose states are cleanly separable. Where the two disagree, ICL is the safer default.

The parameter count is quadratic in K. At 10⁵ photons, going from 3 to 4 states adds ≈ 92 to the BIC penalty — the 4-state model must improve lnL by more than ~46 just to break even.

So: a BIC curve that keeps falling is more often unmodelled heterogeneity — photophysics, bleaching, aggregates — than real extra conformations.

steps.title: Restarts and the seed are the reproducibility check
steps.text:
Baum-Welch increases the likelihood monotonically — to a local optimum. The likelihood is multimodal, so the answer depends on where the fit started.

That is what the restarts are for, and why the seed is exposed: the same seed refits to the same answer, so a result can be reported and reproduced, and a different seed draws an independent set of starting points. Agreement across seeds is the evidence that the optimum is global. It is a check to run, not something to assume.

Expect label permutation: state 1 and state 2 may swap between runs. Match states by E, never by index.

steps.title: The decoder is a separate choice, and it changes the answer
steps.text:
Viterbi maximises the probability of a whole sequence. That is right for one trajectory and wrong for an occupancy or a per-state decay, which ask how many photons belong to each state.

If every photon has posterior γ = (0.7, 0.3), Viterbi assigns all of them to state 0 — the 30 % is erased. Well-separated states come out inflated, ambiguous ones can vanish.

ffbs draws a whole trajectory from the posterior, so it reproduces the photon distribution and keeps the dwell structure. jitter draws each photon independently: faithful per photon, but it shreds dwells, so ChiSurf takes dwells from a Viterbi path anyway and records that it did.

Ticking write puts the assignment back into the photon stream — a PTU whose routing channels encode (stream, state), plus a sidecar. A per-state decay or FCS then becomes an ordinary channel selection in any tool.

steps.title: Fit
steps.text:
Each state count in the range is fitted with the chosen number of restarts, the criterion is evaluated, and the winning model is decoded. A scan with restarts runs for minutes — ⏹ stops it.

Scan patience stops the scan early once the criterion starts rising, which is safe and roughly 1.6× faster; set it to off to fit every state count regardless.

steps.title: Read the dashboard, then test the model
steps.text:
Model selection first — if the criterion has not turned, the state count is not settled and nothing else on the dashboard is worth reading.
Dwell FRET / Transition density: where the states are and which ones exchange.
Dwell times: should be exponential with the state's exit rate — a direct check on the transition matrix. But every dwell is truncated by its burst, which biases the distribution short and the rates high; the first and last dwell of each burst are censored by construction, so drop them with the Is Edge flag in the per-dwell table.
Transition rates: the kinetic scheme itself, and the number to quote.

Then ± (bootstrap) and 📈 (likelihood scan) put confidence intervals on each state. A flat profile or a window-wide interval means the data do not determine that state — no amount of refitting will fix it.

One last thing: the per-state E is an apparent proximity ratio. No leakage, no direct excitation, no γ. Correct it before comparing with anything.

The ? button has the rest.
